items.markdown:
To treat eczema, use thick, fragrance-free [Moisturizers](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/9998-eczema) applied to damp skin after a short, lukewarm bath.

### Daily Skincare

- **Soak and seal:** Take a 5-to-10-minute bath or shower in warm water, then gently pat dry and apply cream or ointment within three minutes.
- **Moisturize often:** Apply a thick, fragrance-free cream or ointment multiple times a day to repair your skin barrier.
- **Avoid harsh soaps:** Use mild, dye-free, and fragrance-free cleansers instead of strong soaps.[[1]](https://nationaleczema.org/treatments/)[[2]](https://www.aad.org/news/how-to-treat-eczema-at-home)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RoyJQVsQ2ZQ&t=1)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=21BzjhJ2Xtw&t=7)

### Medications

- **Topical steroids:** Apply over-the-counter hydrocortisone 1% or prescription-strength topical corticosteroids to calm redness and swelling.
- **Non-steroidal topicals:** Use prescription options like calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus) or JAK inhibitors if steroids are not ideal.
- **Oral treatments:** Take antihistamines for nighttime itch relief or talk to a doctor about systemic or biologic drugs for severe cases.[[1]](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/atopic-dermatitis-eczema/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20353279)[[2]](https://www.goodrx.com/conditions/eczema/current-treatments-mild-severe-eczema)[[3]](https://nyulangone.org/conditions/eczema-dermatitis/treatments/medication-for-eczema-dermatitis)[[4]](https://www.oakderm.com/dermatology-blog/what-is-the-fastest-way-to-heal-eczema)[[5]](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/eczema/types/atopic-dermatitis/treatment)[[6]](https://www.nationaljewish.org/conditions/eczema/eczema-treatment)

### Trigger Management

- **Wear soft fabrics:** Choose loose, 100% cotton clothing and avoid wool or rough synthetic materials.
- **Control your environment:** Protect your skin from extreme heat or cold and use gentle, fragrance-free laundry detergents.
- **Manage stress:** Practice relaxation techniques, as stress can trigger or worsen flare-ups.[[1]](https://www.aad.org/news/how-to-treat-eczema-at-home)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=21BzjhJ2Xtw&t=7)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T_HbQo5oWak&t=4)[[4]](https://www.dermatologyworcester.com/post/at-home-remedies-to-control-eczema-triggers)

- Is the eczema for an **adult or a child**?
- What **parts of the body** are affected?

I can give you more specific advice or help you decide when to see a doctor.
